Sentence (English): I bought the 604 Kitchenaid dishwasher (D), and it is amazing.
Comments (English): [ Great Choice for my Family ] || ---------------- || I bought the 604 Kitchenaid dishwasher (D), and it is amazing. I am 60 years old and I have had many many D in my 40 year marriage, but this one is the best with the 3rd rack that holds cups and glasses! (I load mugs in the middle tray) We are a family of 4 and I run 1 load every single day of the week! Before I used to load my D and then be left with extra items, then I used to have to re-adjust the items I already loaded to try to fit in the items that were still outside the D. It felt like a puzzle trying to make everything fit. Not anymore, I load it and usually I simply run it on "Pro Wash". The directions say I do NOT need to rinse my dishes. But I am in the habit of rinsing every item before I load it, most likely because I always felt my previous D did not do an excellent job. I have used the Kitchenaid D for 1 month, and every item is sparkling clean after the cycle! Before, once in awhile, I used to get an item that was not 100% clean, so I would need to lightly scrub and rewash in the next cycle. Not anymore. So far, every item has come out 100% spotless. I inspect every single item I pull out of the D! It is very satisfying to have 100% sparking clean items! I have a bedroom right next to the kitchen, and the D is quiet enough not to disturb my daughter. Last Sat, I turned on the D while my husband and I cooked, and the D was quiet enough it did not bother our conversation. I thought I needed a quieter decibel, but even though I have hardwood floors in my home, the noise does not travel out of the kitchen. Noise is really not an issue anymore, and our house is an older 1300 sq ft with mostely and open floor plan. I had to chose between a Bosh that was super at drying and super quiet decibel, but it had a lower load capacity, but for me I need the ability to load everything in 1 load. Mostly I throw in everything including the pots and pans and all plastics. I love to see my kitchen counters clean and empty, I do not even like to have clean dishes drying on the rack, so having the ability to load everything is perfect for me. Noise is not an issue, and if it ever was and issue, the D has a timer so I can run it when I leave to work if I wanted to. But so far, I just run it with no noise problems at all. My only reservation is there is a bit of water on top of the cups sometimes depending on the cup construction, and the tupperware plastics are slightly wet, but I usually use 1 paper towel to slightly wipe these items as I am storing them away, it is not a big deal for me at all. Since the paper towel is wet but clean, I lay it out to dry and reuse it. I hope this is helpful to someone.

Sentence (English): The dishwasher itself cleans and dries well.
Comments (English): [ Washes great, some things I wish I would have know ] || ---------------- || The dishwasher itself cleans and dries well. That's really all you can ask of a dishwasher. However for the price, and the reputation, I did expect a little more. While it's very quiet, which I love, it gives off a strange odor while running. At first I figured it was off gassing but it's been enough time. So I'm not sure what it is but it doesn't seem to harm anything. Secondly, I didn't realize the filter needed to be taken out and cleaned - ideally after every wash. This is an inconvenience because it does take time to clean the filter (I have to use a toothbrush). And if you don't keep it clean then your dishes will come out with food still on them. I really like how I can wash Stanley cups without them getting damaged, and can throw other plastic ware in there and it won't melt. All in all, I'm happy with the purchase but for these issues I wouldn't have paid this much money. I assumed I was getting the best of the best and I think a kitchen aid would have done the job for less money.

Sentence (English): WHY WE SETTLED FOR THIS PARTICULAR MODEL:This was not my first choice of the dishwasher.
Comments (English): [ IT WILL FIT IN THE SMALLER OPENING THEN STANDARD ] || ---------------- || WHY WE SETTLED FOR THIS PARTICULAR MODEL:This was not my first choice of the dishwasher. I do like Samsung brand and I would not mind to buy their higher model of dishwashers but our opening under the counter was at 33.5 " so it was way too small to accommodate a standard size machine of most brands.It is very hard to find a shorter dishwasher that will fit in such space. Samsung happens to have one model and it not only fit, but it fit with a lot of extra space on the top. Any dishwasher that is ADA compliant will do the trick and this one just happens to be ADA compliant.WHAT DO WE SHOULD BUT DID NOT KNOW ABOUT THIS DISHWASHER:So what we missed somehow not due to the fault of ours is the fact that most of not all Asian and European machines are somewhat more user friendly and are way easier to install then most American models, they do not require any much electrical skills because they come with the cord with plug so all you have to do is plug them to the 110V outlet and you are good to go. Nice? Yes. If you happen to have a dedicated outlet installed under the sink. Celebrate! We did not have one. That added roughly 300 dollars on the top of standard installation AND delayed the process of installation by few days because the guys who came with the machine, however nice, were not certified to install any such outlet so we had to send them back and get electrician to install the outlet.With the said outlet it is not a rocket science because you already have wiring running for your current dishwasher so all there is to do is to pull the wire and install the outlet under the sink. Thusly you will enjoy your dedicated outlet. It has to be an outlet of a special kind, boxy and safe with grounding and such but I am sure the current dishwasher you had already had an appropriate line so the electrician will just install the outlet. Do not fall for the trick that you need a special separate line pulled from your motherboard if you already had a dishwasher. Some electric places equated us we needed that which was not true.So once you have your outlet installed you are ready to install the dishwasher that will now need only hook up to the water line and the food disposer if you have one. The dishwasher comes with the plastic hose attached to it so you just hook the other end to the disposer. The water line is a flexible metal woven cord that your old dishwasher probably has and you can see it running it from your hot water line under the sink to your old dishwasher. You will need a new water cord for that. I recommend getting it form local Home Depot store as it is cheaper then from Samsung and you can decide how long your hose need to be.After all this experience we think that it is much smarter to have your outlet installed PRIOR to the purchase or at least the delivery of the machine as this way you will be ready for the simple water /sewage hookup and will save yourself time and frustration. Also it would be MUCH nicer of Samsung to note somewhere where we buyers can easily see that this dishwasher requires such an outlet as it is kind of plug and play device from the perspective of electricity at least. Is it nice? Yes, will it be useful in the future? That depends what kind of dishwasher you will get, if American, then you will need to reverse the process, if European or Asian then you are good to go.So again - Dear Samsung, please save us customer frustration and help us plan ahead so installation can be timely, and frustration free. Thank you! WHAT DO WE LIKE ABOUT THIS DISHWASHER:Stainless inside tube - that was our priority. Before anything else it had to be stainless interior and so it is.Sanitizing cycle - we have pets and kids at home so we like to have all our dishes sanitized promptly so that was an absolute must. Hot wash cycle - since the dishes wash much easier and better in hot cycle then this was something we hoped for and it was granted. Heat drying - absolute must. Many of high end dishwashers tend to have air drying system that somewhat differs. I am not an expert on those things but I really wanted some heating element to heat air in the machine so the dishes come very dry and very warm. That is added comfort when unloading nice warm dishes and also added comfort that dishes are additionally sterilized by heat.Front control panel - Our previous machine was top of the line GE model with controls on the top that were hidden when machine was closed, something of the standards of the time back when we were buying it.While the controls on the top may be bit easier to see and press as you are standing as you can see what you are pressing which is not possible with the front controls I much rather prefer this model to the previous one if not for anything else then for the fact that I can see VERY clearly what I am pressing as digits and images are much larger and also I can ALWAYS tell if the machine is in use or not and if it is working how much time is left to the end of the cycle. No more guessing! Overall the front panel is VERY WELL design. It has all the features set in a simple manner, easy to use and understand and you don't need any manuals to run the dishwasher even if you have never seen it before and have nobody to explain it to you.While it does not have as many cycles or features as our old top of the line over 1000 GEmodel it also has everything I need as most of those features I paid for neither I nor anyone else was using or cared about.Half load cycle - yes, it has it and I really need and want it as sometimes I just need to run quickly a half load and so it is great to have.It has Pots and Pans cycle - sure, of course, I will take it. I need it.Aside from this, the time of even the longest cycle is so much more logical because on the Heavy pots WITH sanitizing turned on (yes you can add sanitize to any cycle! ) it is about 3 hours. while without the Sanitizeit is about 2.5 hour give or take few minutes. So that is great.LEARNING CURVE:Our old GE model had a VERY heavy front door full of electronics, nothing like Samsung so when I open I am surprised each and every time how light it is and how little force you need to open it. It is a good thing but needs mental adjusting.NORMAL REGULAR SIZE DINNER PLATES WILL NOT FIT ON THE BOTTOM DRAWER! Ha! I have not seen this coming? Again Dear Samsung, it is not deal breaker when someone is pressed to buy your short lovely machine but leaving it off the description makes you look like bit less transparent then I would like. So no, the normal, standard dinner plates of some 11" or so give or take as they run the gamut here in the US. they WILL NOT FIT the bottom drawer. no the loading alone is not a problem because you can fit them just fine! The problem is that the beautiful arm spraying water from the top on them can not move freely and will get instantly stuck upon program initiation. Nothing as high as the plate can be put there either as it will meet the same fate. You will learn it in two ways. either you will see that dishes come out dirty and wonder why? or you will hear little click click sound or not and will wonder what is it and upon investigation you will figure it out. My old good habit saved me as my old machine also had upper spray arm so I always checked if it moves around freely after loading the load and before closing the door. I tend to bake too so some of the pots or baking stuff can be taller so placing them in the lower drawer required some finesse and acrobatics to make sure the arm moves. But do not cry! the plates can and will be washed just fine! All you have to do is to place them in the UPPER drawer. They will be bit tilted but fit just fine and get cleaned to perfection.I don't mind at all to have the reversed situation here when the upper rack carry the taller load and it is fine with me. It is just that it will require bit of use-to using :)We have this machine for about two weeks and I run many loads, more then needed in actuality as I wanted to test it well and make sure it does good job before we settle for it.THE SPIKESNot sure what is the name of those pointy thingies that separate dishes within the drawer. so they are way shorter then in standard machines, about half the height? maybe? and so sometimes they do bit lesser job holding things that are heavier or angled however I am still learning the strategy and so far I like machine enough to make myself compromise here. I would like them to be higher but perhaps due to the fact that this machine is ADA compliant therefore must serve People with Disabilities this must be the reason and priority so for the greater good it is totally non issue to get used to shorter prangs if it helps other people in their daily lives.BOTTOM LINEThe machine is perfect for our needs, it has all the cycles we need and does not have any thing we don't so we did not have to pay for them. It looks great in our kitchen and the display shows the time of the cycle so we don't need to guess how much time left to the end of the cycle. The plates and big dishes and pots can fit in just fine but taller thing may need to go on the top instead of the bottom.The machine looks great and does perfect job of making dishes clean. The rinsing is absolutely perfect and dishes come out clean and spotless. So this machine has all I wanted and needed in a dishwasher.I just would like Samsung to somehow make up to a customer for the fact that they fail to informthat the electric outlet will be needed prior to installation and the fact that the lower rack will not hold standard plates.

Nice? Yes. If you happen to have a dedicated outlet installed under the sink. Celebrate! We did not have one. That added roughly 300 dollars on the top of standard installation AND delayed the process of installation by few days  because the guys who came with the machine, however nice, were not certified to install any such outlet so we had to send them back and get electrician to install the outlet.With the said outlet it is not a rocket science because you already have wiring running for your current dishwasher so all there is to do is to pull the wire and install the outlet under the sink. Thusly you will enjoy your dedicated outlet. It has to be an outlet of a special kind, boxy and safe with grounding and such but I am sure the current dishwasher you had already had an appropriate line so the electrician will just install the outlet. Do not fall for the trick that you need a special separate line pulled from your motherboard if you already had a dishwasher. Some electric places equated us we  needed that which was not true.So once you have your outlet installed you are ready to install the dishwasher that will now need only hook up to the water line and the food disposer if you have one. The dishwasher comes with the plastic hose attached to it so you just hook the other end to the disposer. The water line is a flexible metal woven cord that your old dishwasher probably has and you can see it running it from your hot water line under the sink to  your old dishwasher. You will need a new water cord for that. I recommend getting it form local Home Depot store as it is cheaper then from Samsung and you can decide how long your hose need to be.After all this experience we think that it is much smarter to have your outlet installed PRIOR to the purchase or at least the delivery of the machine as this way you will be ready for the simple water /sewage hookup and will save yourself time and frustration. Also it would be MUCH nicer of Samsung to note somewhere where we buyers can easily see that this dishwasher requires such an outlet as it is kind of plug and play device from the perspective of electricity at least. Is it nice? Yes, will it be useful in the future? Thank you!WHAT DO WE  LIKE ABOUT THIS DISHWASHER:Stainless inside tube - that was our priority. Before anything else it had to be stainless interior and so it is.Sanitizing cycle - we have pets and kids at home so we like to have all our dishes sanitized promptly so that was an absolute must. Nice? Yes. If you happen to have a dedicated outlet installed under the sink. Celebrate! We did not have one. That added roughly 300 dollars on the top of standard installation AND delayed the process of installation by few days  because the guys who came with the machine, however nice, were not certified to install any such outlet so we had to send them back and get electrician to install the outlet.With the said outlet it is not a rocket science because you already have wiring running for your current dishwasher so all there is to do is to pull the wire and install the outlet under the sink. Thusly you will enjoy your dedicated outlet. It has to be an outlet of a special kind, boxy and safe with grounding and such but I am sure the current dishwasher you had already had an appropriate line so the electrician will just install the outlet. Do not fall for the trick that you need a special separate line pulled from your motherboard if you already had a dishwasher. Some electric places equated us we  needed that which was not true.So once you have your outlet installed you are ready to install the dishwasher that will now need only hook up to the water line and the food disposer if you have one. The dishwasher comes with the plastic hose attached to it so you just hook the other end to the disposer. The water line is a flexible metal woven cord that your old dishwasher probably has and you can see it running it from your hot water line under the sink to  your old dishwasher. You will need a new water cord for that. I recommend getting it form local Home Depot store as it is cheaper then from Samsung and you can decide how long your hose need to be.After all this experience we think that it is much smarter to have your outlet installed PRIOR to the purchase or at least the delivery of the machine as this way you will be ready for the simple water /sewage hookup and will save yourself time and frustration. Also it would be MUCH nicer of Samsung to note somewhere where we buyers can easily see that this dishwasher requires such an outlet as it is kind of plug and play device from the perspective of electricity at least. Is it nice? Yes, will it be useful in the future? That depends what kind of dishwasher you will get, if American, then you will need to reverse the process, if European or Asian then you are good to go.So again - Dear Samsung, please save us customer frustration and help us plan ahead so installation can be timely, and frustration free. Thank you!WHAT DO WE  LIKE ABOUT THIS DISHWASHER:Stainless inside tube - that was our priority. Before anything else it had to be stainless interior and so it is.Sanitizing cycle - we have pets and kids at home so we like to have all our dishes sanitized promptly so that was an absolute must. Nice? Yes. If you happen to have a dedicated outlet installed under the sink. Celebrate! We did not have one. Thusly you will enjoy your dedicated outlet. It has to be an outlet of a special kind, boxy and safe with grounding and such but I am sure the current dishwasher you had already had an appropriate line so the electrician will just install the outlet. Some electric places equated us we  needed that which was not true.So once you have your outlet installed you are ready to install the dishwasher that will now need only hook up to the water line and the food disposer if you have one. The water line is a flexible metal woven cord that your old dishwasher probably has and you can see it running it from your hot water line under the sink to  your old dishwasher. You will need a new water cord for that. I recommend getting it form local Home Depot store as it is cheaper then from Samsung and you can decide how long your hose need to be.After all this experience we think that it is much smarter to have your outlet installed PRIOR to the purchase or at least the delivery of the machine as this way you will be ready for the simple water /sewage hookup and will save yourself time and frustration. Is it nice? Yes, will it be useful in the future? Thank you!WHAT DO WE  LIKE ABOUT THIS DISHWASHER:Stainless inside tube - that was our priority. So this machine has all I wanted and needed in a dishwasher.I just would like Samsung to somehow make up to a customer for the fact that they fail to informthat the electric outlet will be needed prior to installation and the fact that the lower rack will not hold standard plates.

Nice? Yes. If you happen to have a dedicated outlet installed under the sink. Celebrate! We did not have one. That added roughly 300 dollars on the top of standard installation AND delayed the process of installation by few days  because the guys who came with the machine, however nice, were not certified to install any such outlet so we had to send them back and get electrician to install the outlet.With the said outlet it is not a rocket science because you already have wiring running for your current dishwasher so all there is to do is to pull the wire and install the outlet under the sink. Thusly you will enjoy your dedicated outlet. It has to be an outlet of a special kind, boxy and safe with grounding and such but I am sure the current dishwasher you had already had an appropriate line so the electrician will just install the outlet. Do not fall for the trick that you need a special separate line pulled from your motherboard if you already had a dishwasher. Some electric places equated us we  needed that which was not true.So once you have your outlet installed you are ready to install the dishwasher that will now need only hook up to the water line and the food disposer if you have one. The dishwasher comes with the plastic hose attached to it so you just hook the other end to the disposer. The water line is a flexible metal woven cord that your old dishwasher probably has and you can see it running it from your hot water line under the sink to  your old dishwasher. You will need a new water cord for that. I recommend getting it form local Home Depot store as it is cheaper then from Samsung and you can decide how long your hose need to be.After all this experience we think that it is much smarter to have your outlet installed PRIOR to the purchase or at least the delivery of the machine as this way you will be ready for the simple water /sewage hookup and will save yourself time and frustration. Also it would be MUCH nicer of Samsung to note somewhere where we buyers can easily see that this dishwasher requires such an outlet as it is kind of plug and play device from the perspective of electricity at least. Is it nice? Yes, will it be useful in the future? That depends what kind of dishwasher you will get, if American, then you will need to reverse the process, if European or Asian then you are good to go.So again - Dear Samsung, please save us customer frustration and help us plan ahead so installation can be timely, and frustration free. Thank you!WHAT DO WE  LIKE ABOUT THIS DISHWASHER:Stainless inside tube - that was our priority. Before anything else it had to be stainless interior and so it is.Sanitizing cycle - we have pets and kids at home so we like to have all our dishes sanitized promptly so that was an absolute must. Hot wash cycle - since the dishes wash much easier and better in hot cycle then this was something we hoped for and it was granted. Heat drying - absolute must. Many of high end dishwashers tend to have air drying system that somewhat differs. I am not an expert on those things but I really wanted some heating element to heat air in the machine so the dishes come very dry and very warm. No more guessing!Overall the front panel is VERY WELL design. It has all the features set in a simple manner, easy to use and understand and you don't need any manuals to run the dishwasher even if you have never seen it before and have nobody to explain it to you.While it does not have as many cycles or features as our old top of the line over 1000 GEmodel it also has everything I need as most of those features I paid for neither I nor anyone else was using or cared about.Half load cycle - yes, it has it and I really need and want it as sometimes I just need to run quickly a half load and so it is great to have.It has Pots and Pans cycle - sure, of course, I will take it. So no, the normal, standard dinner plates of some 11' or so give or take as they run the gamut here in the US.. they WILL NOT FIT the bottom drawer..  no the loading alone is not a problem because you can fit them just fine! You will learn it in two ways.. either you will see that dishes come out dirty and wonder why? or you will hear little click click sound or not and will wonder what is it and upon investigation you will figure it out. So this machine has all I wanted and needed in a dishwasher.I just would like Samsung to somehow make up to a customer for the fact that they fail to informthat the electric outlet will be needed prior to installation and the fact that the lower rack will not hold standard plates.

Nice? Yes. If you happen to have a dedicated outlet installed under the sink. Celebrate! We did not have one. That added roughly 300 dollars on the top of standard installation AND delayed the process of installation by few days  because the guys who came with the machine, however nice, were not certified to install any such outlet so we had to send them back and get electrician to install the outlet.With the said outlet it is not a rocket science because you already have wiring running for your current dishwasher so all there is to do is to pull the wire and install the outlet under the sink. Thusly you will enjoy your dedicated outlet. It has to be an outlet of a special kind, boxy and safe with grounding and such but I am sure the current dishwasher you had already had an appropriate line so the electrician will just install the outlet. Do not fall for the trick that you need a special separate line pulled from your motherboard if you already had a dishwasher. Some electric places equated us we  needed that which was not true.So once you have your outlet installed you are ready to install the dishwasher that will now need only hook up to the water line and the food disposer if you have one. The dishwasher comes with the plastic hose attached to it so you just hook the other end to the disposer. The water line is a flexible metal woven cord that your old dishwasher probably has and you can see it running it from your hot water line under the sink to  your old dishwasher. You will need a new water cord for that. I recommend getting it form local Home Depot store as it is cheaper then from Samsung and you can decide how long your hose need to be.After all this experience we think that it is much smarter to have your outlet installed PRIOR to the purchase or at least the delivery of the machine as this way you will be ready for the simple water /sewage hookup and will save yourself time and frustration. Also it would be MUCH nicer of Samsung to note somewhere where we buyers can easily see that this dishwasher requires such an outlet as it is kind of plug and play device from the perspective of electricity at least. Is it nice? Yes, will it be useful in the future? That depends what kind of dishwasher you will get, if American, then you will need to reverse the process, if European or Asian then you are good to go.So again - Dear Samsung, please save us customer frustration and help us plan ahead so installation can be timely, and frustration free. Thank you!WHAT DO WE  LIKE ABOUT THIS DISHWASHER:Stainless inside tube - that was our priority. Before anything else it had to be stainless interior and so it is.Sanitizing cycle - we have pets and kids at home so we like to have all our dishes sanitized promptly so that was an absolute must. Hot wash cycle - since the dishes wash much easier and better in hot cycle then this was something we hoped for and it was granted. Heat drying - absolute must. Many of high end dishwashers tend to have air drying system that somewhat differs. I am not an expert on those things but I really wanted some heating element to heat air in the machine so the dishes come very dry and very warm. No more guessing!Overall the front panel is VERY WELL design. It has all the features set in a simple manner, easy to use and understand and you don't need any manuals to run the dishwasher even if you have never seen it before and have nobody to explain it to you.While it does not have as many cycles or features as our old top of the line over 1000 GEmodel it also has everything I need as most of those features I paid for neither I nor anyone else was using or cared about.Half load cycle - yes, it has it and I really need and want it as sometimes I just need to run quickly a half load and so it is great to have.It has Pots and Pans cycle - sure, of course, I will take it. I need it.Aside from this, the time of even the longest cycle is so much more logical because on the Heavy pots WITH sanitizing turned on (yes you can add sanitize to any cycle!)  it is about 3 hours.. while without the Sanitizeit is about 2.5 hour give or take few minutes. So no, the normal, standard dinner plates of some 11' or so give or take as they run the gamut here in the US.. they WILL NOT FIT the bottom drawer..  no the loading alone is not a problem because you can fit them just fine! You will learn it in two ways.. either you will see that dishes come out dirty and wonder why? or you will hear little click click sound or not and will wonder what is it and upon investigation you will figure it out. So this machine has all I wanted and needed in a dishwasher.I just would like Samsung to somehow make up to a customer for the fact that they fail to informthat the electric outlet will be needed prior to installation and the fact that the lower rack will not hold standard plates.

Thusly you will enjoy your dedicated outlet. It has to be an outlet of a special kind, boxy and safe with grounding and such but I am sure the current dishwasher you had already had an appropriate line so the electrician will just install the outlet. Do not fall for the trick that you need a special separate line pulled from your motherboard if you already had a dishwasher. On the flip side, it gets my dishes 10000x cleaner than that GE did even when it was brand new. So again, maybe it's not a con that it holds less. I just need to get used to doing dishes a bit more frequently.

Sentence (English): I bought this dishwasher in 2021.
Comments (English): [ Loved the dishwasher, but it didn't last long. ] || ---------------- || I bought this dishwasher in 2021. It was a quiet, well performing dishwasher that had ample space, useful racks that could be raised/ lowered and had foldable tines, and had a really nice overnight drying feature which I loved. There was a minor material issue where some of the coating on the dish racks came away and it started to rust, but we're talking less than 0.25 inches in size, and it didn't affect performance so it didn't bother me. What did drive the 2 star review is that after 3 years, the dishwasher started making a loud whining sound and it would take an extra hour to go through the cleaning cycle. Normally not a problem since I ran it at night, and everything was clean in the end. A little more than 2 months later, it stopped working altogether. The circulation pump stopped working, and it needed repair or replacement. I called LG, and was underwhelmed with their lack of helpfulness. They did give me a list of technicians i can contact, but I'll be responsible for paying. Though they didn't specify if I'd pay for just the service, or the pump as well, they did leave me with the impression I would have to pay for the whole thing. No rebate, no apology. They just didn't try to help me, since it was after 3 years. It was no longer under warranty. Reading other reviews, some have also experienced a circulation pump failure after about 3 years. This leads me to believe that this is not a random event, but a weakness with the product itself. Since it was close to Thanksgiving, I didn't decide to repair it or fight it. I needed a dishwasher, so I went and bought a different brand. I lost trust with LG products as a result of this experience, and I'll be hard pressed to buy another appliance from them.

It was a quiet, well performing dishwasher that had ample space, useful racks that could be raised/ lowered and had foldable tines, and had a really nice overnight drying feature which I loved. There was a minor material issue where some of the coating on the dish racks came away and it started to rust, but we're talking less than 0.25 inches in size, and it didn't affect performance so it didn't bother me. What did drive the 2 star review is that after 3 years, the dishwasher started making a loud whining sound and it would take an extra hour to go through the cleaning cycle. Normally not a problem since I ran it at night, and everything was clean in the end. A little more than 2 months later, it stopped working altogether. The circulation pump stopped working, and it needed repair or replacement. I called LG, and was underwhelmed with their lack of helpfulness. They did give me a list of technicians i can contact, but I'll be responsible for paying. Though they didn't specify if I'd pay for just the service, or the pump as well, they did leave me with the impression I would have to pay for the whole thing. No rebate, no apology. They just didn't try to help me, since it was after 3 years. It was no longer under warranty. Reading other reviews, some have also experienced a circulation pump failure after about 3 years. This leads me to believe that this is not a random event, but a weakness with the product itself. Since it was close to Thanksgiving, I didn't decide to repair it or fight it. I needed a dishwasher, so I went and bought a different brand. I lost trust with LG products as a result of this experience, and I'll be hard pressed to buy another appliance from them.

Sentence (English): Overall, my Costco-purchased 800 series Bosch DW is a powerful, quiet, well-thought-out machine.
Comments (English): [ Quality Machine - Cleaning is Good, Not Improved ] || ---------------- || Overall, my Costco-purchased 800 series Bosch DW is a powerful, quiet, well-thought-out machine. However, I have two points of feedback.First, there is likely no avoiding it in high-end DWs (seems to be the way the industry is going), but I am not a fan on the third-rack for utensils. My flatwear is not getting cleaner by being spaced-out in their own dedicated holders and who in their right-mind would choose to take all the time and steps (pull-out the third rack, pick a placement that efficiently uses the available space among other utensils, click-in a single fork/knife/spoon, push the third-rack back to the closed position so you can continue loading dishes) when the alternative of simply tossing utensils into a basket worked perfectly and was so much faster? Second, I have trouble with very large format wine glasses coming out with grit on them, which was not a problem with my prior Bosch DW. I have figured out that placing these large wine glasses in the center of the bottom rack (they don't come close to fitting on the middle rack. thanks to the lost height due to the third-rack), yields a higher success rate. However, this is not a great use of bottom rack space, there are often heavy pots/pans nearby that could break the wine glasses, and I often have more large wine glasses that must sit on the counter and wait for a future load, as I can't put them around the parameter of the bottom rack and have them come out clean.

Comments (English): [ Bosch 500 Series problems ] || ---------------- || This is the 2nd Bosch 500 series dishwasher we have owned, the 1st one needing replacement after owning it for only 4.5 years due to a leak (error code E15) that one Bosch authorized technician stated would cost $700 to repair and a 2nd Bosch authorized technician could not resolve after coming to our house three times. Issue #1 - 5 days after the current dishwasher was installed, it stopped getting power. The installer had to return to replace the dishwasher's electical plug and cable. Issue #2, the door when working properly is designed to open to allow the moisture to vent helping the dishes to dry more completely when using the Air Dry setting. About 1 week after the plug issue was resolved, the door started opening only about 1/8 of an inch instead of the proper 1.5-2.0 inches at the end of the dry cycle causing moisture in the dishwasher to gather just under the lip of the counter and on the top of the dishwasher door and then drip onto the floor.

UV램프와 자동문열림 기능은 위생과 편의성을 모두 잡은 점에서 큰 장점이며, 방문설치 서비스까지 더해져 사용 경험이 매우 만족스러웠어요.●●●●●●●●●●●●●●●●●●●●●●●●●●●●리뷰는 여기서 마치도록 하겠습니다.구매에 도움이 되었으면 좋겠어요.오늘도 좋은 하루되시고, 합리적인 소비하시길 바라요. :)

UV램프와 자동문열림 기능은 위생과 편의성을 모두 잡은 점에서 큰 장점이며, 방문설치 서비스까지 더해져 사용 경험이 매우 만족스러웠어요.●●●●●●●●●●●●●●●●●●●●●●●●●●●●리뷰는 여기서 마치도록 하겠습니다.구매에 도움이 되었으면 좋겠어요.오늘도 좋은 하루되시고, 합리적인 소비하시길 바라요. :)

UV램프와 자동문열림 기능은 위생과 편의성을 모두 잡은 점에서 큰 장점이며, 방문설치 서비스까지 더해져 사용 경험이 매우 만족스러웠어요.●●●●●●●●●●●●●●●●●●●●●●●●●●●●리뷰는 여기서 마치도록 하겠습니다.구매에 도움이 되었으면 좋겠어요.오늘도 좋은 하루되시고, 합리적인 소비하시길 바라요. :)

UV램프와 자동문열림 기능은 위생과 편의성을 모두 잡은 점에서 큰 장점이며, 방문설치 서비스까지 더해져 사용 경험이 매우 만족스러웠어요.●●●●●●●●●●●●●●●●●●●●●●●●●●●●리뷰는 여기서 마치도록 하겠습니다.구매에 도움이 되었으면 좋겠어요.오늘도 좋은 하루되시고, 합리적인 소비하시길 바라요. :)

UV램프와 자동문열림 기능은 위생과 편의성을 모두 잡은 점에서 큰 장점이며, 방문설치 서비스까지 더해져 사용 경험이 매우 만족스러웠어요.●●●●●●●●●●●●●●●●●●●●●●●●●●●●리뷰는 여기서 마치도록 하겠습니다.구매에 도움이 되었으면 좋겠어요.오늘도 좋은 하루되시고, 합리적인 소비하시길 바라요. :)

UV램프와 자동문열림 기능은 위생과 편의성을 모두 잡은 점에서 큰 장점이며, 방문설치 서비스까지 더해져 사용 경험이 매우 만족스러웠어요.●●●●●●●●●●●●●●●●●●●●●●●●●●●●리뷰는 여기서 마치도록 하겠습니다.구매에 도움이 되었으면 좋겠어요.오늘도 좋은 하루되시고, 합리적인 소비하시길 바라요. :)

UV램프와 자동문열림 기능은 위생과 편의성을 모두 잡은 점에서 큰 장점이며, 방문설치 서비스까지 더해져 사용 경험이 매우 만족스러웠어요.●●●●●●●●●●●●●●●●●●●●●●●●●●●●리뷰는 여기서 마치도록 하겠습니다.구매에 도움이 되었으면 좋겠어요.오늘도 좋은 하루되시고, 합리적인 소비하시길 바라요. :)

UV램프와 자동문열림 기능은 위생과 편의성을 모두 잡은 점에서 큰 장점이며, 방문설치 서비스까지 더해져 사용 경험이 매우 만족스러웠어요.●●●●●●●●●●●●●●●●●●●●●●●●●●●●리뷰는 여기서 마치도록 하겠습니다.구매에 도움이 되었으면 좋겠어요.오늘도 좋은 하루되시고, 합리적인 소비하시길 바라요. :)

UV램프와 자동문열림 기능은 위생과 편의성을 모두 잡은 점에서 큰 장점이며, 방문설치 서비스까지 더해져 사용 경험이 매우 만족스러웠어요.●●●●●●●●●●●●●●●●●●●●●●●●●●●●리뷰는 여기서 마치도록 하겠습니다.구매에 도움이 되었으면 좋겠어요.오늘도 좋은 하루되시고, 합리적인 소비하시길 바라요. :)

Sentence (English): After giving birth this year, my mom gifted me a Samsung dishwasher!
Comments (English): [ I should have bought this sooner! I am very satisfied with this dishwasher. ] || ---------------- || After giving birth this year, my mom gifted me a Samsung dishwasher! I used to be the type of person who stubbornly insisted I didn't need a dishwasher because I don't use many dishes; I just wash whatever can be rinsed with water right after meals. But I should have bought one sooner! Pregnant women, newlyweds preparing for pregnancy, and everyone starting parenting—make sure to hire a "Dishwasher Lady" before you start parenting. Why put off something this convenient? (Words I say to my past self). < Review after one month of use > Pros: 1. A life with evenings free is now possible. Before, either my husband or I would spend 30 minutes to an hour in the kitchen after dinner, but now we can put all the dishes in the dishwasher, spend only 5-10 minutes tidying up, and then go for an evening walk or watch Netflix. 2. My back used to hurt doing the dishes, and it felt pitiful to see my tall husband bending over to wash them—now, that need has been reduced by a factor of 1/10. No more back pain, and no more feeling sorry for my husband! 3. They say using the dishwasher saves more water. 4. Samsung dishwashers automatically open the lid after washing, so there is no risk of secondary contamination from water remaining inside! This is why everyone says Samsung dishwashers are better than other brands. 5. Although the hot air drying function has been removed from the recently released models, it actually saves more electricity. Even without hot air drying, the dishwasher runs completely, and even if I leave the lid open for less than an hour, the dishes, cutlery, and cups are all dry. 6. I am satisfied with the quick installation and the trustworthy service provided by the Samsung technician. It was great that they installed it and explained how to use it before leaving. They even gave detailed tips, such as telling me to use the detergent-free sterilization mode after about 40 uses. 7. Since it can wash even fragile wine glasses, I use delicate glass cups, and they haven't broken. 8. Beautiful design! I was debating between beige and white, but since my refrigerator has beige, I chose beige. It is subtle and pretty, so I am satisfied. Even though it has only been a month, I don't get tired of it at all, which is great. 9. Even my cherished dishes are washed safely without damage. Comments (English): [ Great upgrade. ] || ---------------- || I normally don't post reviews but our experience was such an improvement since the last time we ordered appliances from Best Buy that I felt I needed to share. Annette from the Warwick Best Buy was fantastic in helping us find appliances that would work for us and ensuring they got to us as quickly as they could. Our delivery experience for both the dishwasher and refrigerator was also much improved as the appliances arrived undamaged and the technicians were able to answer any questions we had upon delivery. The water, electrical and height adjustments are all at the front of the unit for easy access. The ability to adjust the back legs without having to take the dishwasher out of the space was much appreciated. Overall, we are very happy both with the service we received from Best Buy and with the product itself.
